Q1: Where should the reporter get the Claude pool step reason it passes as `--pool-reason`? (The issue assumes the reporter already reads it, but it does not.)
Choices:
A) Use the same order as `ai_engine_no_account_reason` in `scripts/ai_engine.sh` (lines 246-261). Take `CLAUDE_POOL_REASON` from the environment first. If that is empty, read `CLAUDE_POOL_REASON_FILE` (default `${RUNNER_TEMP}/claude-pool-reason`, written by `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh`), refusing symlinks and reading at most 64 bytes. Add a new local variable in the reporter for it. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Read only the reason file (`CLAUDE_POOL_REASON_FILE` / `${RUNNER_TEMP}/claude-pool-reason`) and ignore the `CLAUDE_POOL_REASON` env var.
C) Read only the `CLAUDE_POOL_REASON` env var. This needs a matching `env:` entry on each workflow's reporter step, which widens scope beyond the four paths the issue lists.
Q2: If no pool reason source exists for the job (no env value and no file, e.g. the pool step never ran), what should the reporter pass?
Choices:
A) Leave out `--pool-reason`, so the payload stays byte-identical to today's. Pass the argument only when a source exists; a value that fails `^[a-z0-9_]{1,60}$` still becomes `unavailable` inside `workflow_failure_heal.py`. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Always pass `--pool-reason`, with an empty value when there is no source. Every engine_fallback payload would then carry `Claude pool step reason: unavailable`.
